img086.png.text: Proximity to a superconductor generally competes with and suppresses the Kondo effect. Cooper-pair (Andreev) correlations induce local pairing on the dots, which screens the spin in a different way (a BCS-like singlet). This reduces the Kondo temperature and the Kondo-related conductance, and the system can shift from a Kondo singlet to a superconducting singlet. When the superconducting gap is large compared to the Kondo scale, the Kondo effect is destroyed. Coupling to the superconductor can also add a new screening channel, so the Kondo screening is modified rather than simply removed.
